notes: §1985:VI.5.15.3 SR3: numeric literals 'must have a value which is within the range of values indicated by the PICTURE clause, and must not have a value which would require truncation of nonzero digits', and 'Nonnumeric literals in a VALUE clause of an item must not exceed the size indicated by the PICTURE clause.' Every item, table-element and condition-name literal (both THRU ends) passes ScreenValueLiteral: ValidateNumericValue refuses truncation of nonzero digits on either side (COBOL1625) and ValidateValueCategory refuses an oversize nonnumeric literal (COBOL1740, numeric edited COBOL1570). The gap of the prior PARTIAL is closed: ValueSubject.ForConditionName now carries the conditional variable's size below 2002 (PB5190), and ScreenGroupConditionName sizes a group's 88 literals. next.reason: The numeric part is kept: §2023:13.18.63.3 SR2 'permissible values within the range indicated by the PICTURE clause ... without truncation of leading or trailing nonzero digits' (its float exceptions cover usages 1985 lacks), and §2023:13.18.63.3 SR6 extends no-truncation to numeric literals for numeric-edited items. The nonnumeric size limit is kept by §2023:13.18.63.3 SR4 only for alphabetic, alphanumeric and alphanumeric-edited items. 1985 limits a nonnumeric literal for ANY item, and numeric edited items take only nonnumeric literals there (§1985:VI.5.15.4 GR1b). 2023 states no size limit for an alphanumeric literal in a numeric-edited item: §2023:13.18.63.3 SR7 constrains only its class. An oversize literal for a numeric-edited item, refused in 1985, is refused by no 2023 rule.
